scope: Named foreign shareholders (≥1%) of five batch-7 constituents (NTPC, ONGC, Power Grid Corporation, SBI Life Insurance, Shriram Finance) from the latest available SEBI Reg. 31(1)(b) quarterly shareholding-pattern filings. Four of five were opened at the primary source: NTPC (dev.ntpc.co.in PDF, quarter ended 30.09.2025), Power Grid (powergrid.in's own HTML rendering of the SEBI XBRL filing, quarter ended 30.09.2025), SBI Life (sbilife.co.in PDF, quarter ended 31.12.2025) and Shriram Finance (cdn.shriramfinance.in PDF, 34-page filing with full named-holder annexures, quarter ended 31.12.2025). ONGC's primary source (ongcindia.com) refused every connection attempted in this pass (repeated TLS/SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL on direct fetch, HTTP 503 on WebFetch) — ONGC rests on a screener.in aggregate only, tier reported, no named holders, with the attempted primary URLs recorded in voids. Three of the five companies (NTPC, ONGC, Power Grid) are majority Government-of-India-owned PSUs with a statutory/practical ceiling on how large any single foreign stake can be while the sovereign promoter holds 51%+; SBI Life's promoter is State Bank of India (a PSU bank, not itself the Government directly) at 55.34%; Shriram Finance is the one private-sector NBFC in the batch and the only one with genuinely large aggregate FPI exposure (47%+) and a pending (not yet completed, and so NOT recorded as a current ownership claim) 20%-stake acquisition by Japan's Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group announced 19 December 2025. Covers: the mandatory comparison set (BlackRock, Vanguard, NBIM/Government Pension Fund Global, GIC/Government of Singapore, Capital Group, Fidelity, Kuwait Investment Authority, ADIA, GQG Partners) tested against all four companies with primary data; LIC of India as the domestic control, present ≥1% in two of four (NTPC, Power Grid) and documented as absent/sub-1% in the other two; two Singapore state entities distinct from GIC found in this batch — Temasek Holdings' wholly-owned vehicle MacRitchie Investments Pte Ltd (SBI Life, non-FPI 'Foreign Companies' category) and the Monetary Authority of Singapore (Shriram Finance, FPI Category I) — both recorded as new holders, not conflated with GIC; and Sanlam Life Insurance Limited, a South African insurer holding a legacy foreign promoter-group FPI stake in Shriram Finance. Leaves out: adviser mandates, SEBI/RBI rule-change history, and the Soros/OSF/World Bank narratives (out of scope for this batch); any company outside the five named above; and the MUFG-Shriram Finance transaction's completion, which had not occurred by the 31.12.2025 filing date this file uses.

voids.what: LIC of India's specific shareholding percentage in SBI Life and in Shriram Finance could not be confirmed as ≥1% from either primary filing. SBI Life's Table III shows an 'Insurance Companies' aggregate of 1.28% across 29 entities with no individual insurer named (consistent with, not proof of, LIC holding under 1% there). voids.whyItMatters: LIC is the domestic-control comparator this file is required to test against every company; its absence (or sub-1% presence) in 2 of the 4 primary-sourced companies in this batch is itself informative — contrasted with LIC's clear >1% presence in the two Government-of-India PSU companies (NTPC 4.94%, Power Grid 3.16%) in the same batch — but is a gap in per-name confirmation, not evidence LIC holds nothing.

symmetryCheck: Run identically across the 5 companies in this batch: LIC of India was found as a large, specifically-named domestic holder in both companies where the promoter is the Government of India directly (NTPC 4.94%, Power Grid 3.16%) — in both cases larger than the entire named-foreign-holder line in the same filing. LIC did NOT appear named ≥1% in the two companies whose promoter is a different domestic institution (SBI, for SBI Life) or a private group (Shriram Capital/Shriram Value Services, for Shriram Finance) — a pattern consistent with LIC concentrating its large stakes in Government-anchored PSUs rather than uniformly across Indian equity. BlackRock/iShares was not found named ≥1% in any of the 4 primary filings opened. Vanguard, Capital Group, Fidelity, Kuwait Investment Authority, ADIA and GQG Partners were likewise absent from all 4. GIC/Government of Singapore was the single most consistently present foreign holder in this batch, named ≥1% in 3 of 4 companies (NTPC 2.04%, Power Grid 2.34%, Shriram Finance 4.66%) — more consistent than any other single comparison-set entity, though every individual line remained well under 5%. This batch also surfaced two Singapore state entities distinct from GIC (Temasek's MacRitchie Investments Pte Ltd in SBI Life, 1.51%; the Monetary Authority of Singapore in Shriram Finance, 1.03%) and NBIM (1.29% of Shriram Finance) — the same 'fragmented, small, multiple sovereign lines rather than one concentrated passive-fund line' structure documented in the earlier holders.json and holders-b6.json files. The structural constraint particular to this batch: three of five companies (NTPC, ONGC, Power Grid) are majority Government-of-India-owned PSUs where the 51%+ statutory/practical promoter floor caps how large ANY single non-promoter holder — foreign or domestic — can mathematically be; this mechanically suppresses both the 'BlackRock owns India' narrative and the 'LIC dominates' narrative to the same degree, which is itself the finding: in PSU-anchored companies the story is sovereign-promoter concentration, not either institutional-investor narrative.
